The '''2019–20 Ligue 1''' season, also known as '''Ligue 1 [[Conforama]]''' for sponsorship reasons, was a French [[association football]] tournament within [[Ligue 1]]. It was the 82nd season since its establishment. The season began on 9 August 2019 and ended abruptly on 28 April 2020.<ref>{{Cite web|title=Season 2019/20 in French Ligue 1 is over|url=https://rowdie.co.uk/article/season-2019-20-in-french-ligue-1-is-over|date=29 April 2020|access-date=28 December 2020|website=rowdie.co.uk}}</ref>

On 13 March 2020, the [[Ligue de Football Professionnel|LFP]] suspended Ligue 1 and [[Ligue 2]] indefinitely following the outbreak of [[COVID-19 pandemic in France|COVID-19 in France]].<ref>{{cite news |url=https://www.lfp.fr/Articles/COMMUNIQUÉS/2020/03/13/communique-de-la-lfp |title=Communiqué de la LFP |website=lfp.fr|publisher=Ligue de Football Professionnel |date=13 March 2020 |access-date=13 March 2020 |language=fr}}</ref> On 28 April 2020, it was announced that Ligue 1 and Ligue 2 campaigns would not resume, after the country banned all sporting events until September.<ref>{{Cite news|url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/52460468|title=Ligue 1 & 2: France's top two divisions will not resume this season|date=28 April 2020|work=BBC Sport|access-date=28 April 2020}}</ref> On 30 April 2020, [[Paris Saint-Germain F.C.|Paris Saint-Germain]] were awarded the championship following the cancellation of the 2019–20 season.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.ligue1.com/Articles/NEWS/2020/04/30/psg-champions-season-ended-ligue-1|title=PSG champions as season ended|date=30 April 2020|access-date=30 April 2020|publisher=Ligue de Football Professionnel|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200501183551/https://www.ligue1.com/Articles/NEWS/2020/04/30/psg-champions-season-ended-ligue-1|archive-date=1 May 2020|url-status=dead}}</ref><ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.bbc.com/sport/football/52484926|title=Ligue 1: Paris St-Germain awarded French title as season finished early|work=BBC Sport|date=30 April 2020|access-date=30 April 2020}}</ref>

PSG topped the standings by 12 points with a game in hand at the time the league was halted. [[Olympique de Marseille|Marseille]] and [[Stade Rennais F.C.|Rennes]] were awarded the other two [[UEFA Champions League]] spots based on their rankings at the league's suspension. On 9 June 2020, France's highest administrative court ruled that relegation for [[Amiens SC|Amiens]] and [[Toulouse FC|Toulouse]] was suspended for this season.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.skysports.com/football/news/11800/12003511/ligue-1-relegation-overruled-for-amiens-and-toulouse-but-lyon-appeal-dismissed|title=Ligue 1 relegation overruled for Amiens and Toulouse but Lyon appeal dismissed|date=9 June 2020|access-date=9 June 2020|work=Sky Sports}}</ref> This was overruled on 23 June and subsequently [[Amiens SC|Amiens]] and [[Toulouse FC|Toulouse]] were relegated to the [[2020–21 Ligue 2]].<ref>{{cite web |title=LFP : l'assemblée générale vote à 74,49 % le maintien d'une Ligue 1 à vingt clubs |url=https://www.lequipe.fr/Football/Actualites/Lfp-l-assemblee-generale-vote-a-74-49-le-maintien-d-une-ligue-1-a-vingt-clubs/1145914 |website=[[L'Équipe]] |access-date=23 June 2020}}</ref>

==Teams==
===Changes===
[[FC Metz|Metz]] and [[Stade Brestois 29|Brest]] were promoted from the [[2018–19 Ligue 2]], replacing the two relegated teams from the [[2018–19 Ligue 1]], [[Stade Malherbe Caen|Caen]] and [[En Avant de Guingamp|Guingamp]].
